RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 25

An all-male panel is not evidence of bias on its own. In senior government grades it often just mirrors who holds those posts. It can raise questions about groupthink or how criteria were weighted, but as a standalone fact it proves nothing and leading with it will likely make you look like you're reaching.

Your stronger ground is substantive: you appear better qualified on paper, the winning candidate's edge rests on a vague phrase ("leading international projects"), and your request for written reasons has been ignored for two weeks. Chase that in writing, cite the relevant deadline, and ask for the scoring against published criteria. If the scores look arbitrary, panel composition becomes context — not the headline.
